anti_overlap: fd-axis-mechanical-distinctness covers whether axes differentiate the current 14-stance set
fd-axis-ideological-authenticity covers whether axes map to real-world recognized positions
fd-axis-orthogonality covers whether axes are independent of each other
decision_lens: Prioritizes axes whose poles become synonymous or meaningless in future scenarios — an axis that perfectly differentiates 2025 energy policy but collapses to a single pole when energy is post-scarcity is a temporal validity failure.
focus: Whether proposed axes remain meaningful and non-degenerate across the 500-year scenario span from 2025 near-term issues through 2525 post-human existential scenarios
name: fd-axis-temporal-validity
persona: A futures studies researcher and game designer who has built long-span historical games (Europa Universalis, Civilization) and thinks carefully about how political categories dissolve and reconstitute over time.
review_areas: For each proposed axis, identify the earliest scenario where the axis would stop producing different gameplay outcomes — scan the issue corpus for temporal markers and test whether the axis still differentiates stance choices

Check the Security domain specifically: Defensive/Aggressive/Diplomatic map cleanly to 2025 geopolitics, but do these stances remain distinct when security threats are synthetic biology releases, AI-driven cyberwar, or consciousness-merging?

Test whether the Labor domain stances (Protect/Deregulate/Mediate) retain meaning when artificial-wombs-and-gestation-outsourcing and automated-companion-replacements dominate — 'labor' as a category may dissolve
Verify that the Governance domain stances (Reform/Infiltrate/Leverage) scale to scenarios with algorithmic-governance-proliferation and consciousness-merger-phenomenon

Examine whether any axis is purely reactive to 21st-century scarcity assumptions: if Technology axis differentiates based on access to computing resources, does it collapse in a post-scarcity compute world?

Check whether the axes can absorb entirely new issue categories not yet represented in the corpus — if a 2400 scenario introduces mind-uploading as a policy domain, does the axis system still classify the player's position?
success_hints: For at least 3 representative issues from each century bracket, the axis should produce a non-degenerate classification

The axis labels should be abstract enough that they describe durable tensions rather than specific policy debates — 'state capacity vs market autonomy' survives longer than 'fossil fuel subsidy vs carbon tax'
task_context: Shadow Work's 353 issue YAML files span from 2025 near-term crises through far-future post-human scenarios. The axis system must classify player behavior coherently across this full span.
